headline: GOLD REBOUNDS to $4,140 after two-week slide — Warsh comments cool October rate-hike odds ahead of Oct 28 FOMC
snippet: Gold spot price recovered to approximately $4,140/oz on October 22 after two consecutive weeks of losses, as remarks by Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh were interpreted by traders as reducing the probability of a rate hike at the October 28 FOMC meeting. Silver followed gold higher, rising roughly 1.3% to $57.73/oz, snapping a four-session losing streak fuelled by oil-driven inflation concerns; the rebound arrives ahead of what analysts describe as a binary FOMC decision for precious metals, with gold needing to hold the $4,000 floor to maintain its multi-year bull structure.

headline: NICKEL SURGES 4.1% to $16,310 on Indonesia NPI cut talk — copper falls as LME inventories swell 8% in one week
snippet: LME nickel jumped 4.1% to $16,310 a tonne — its highest in over three weeks — on reports of possible coordinated production cuts by Chinese nickel pig iron producers operating in Indonesia, including a proposed moratorium on new partly-processed NPI capacity. Meanwhile, three-month LME copper eased 0.4% to $14,364 a tonne as exchange inventories climbed 8% in a week; however over 70% of visible exchange copper stocks sit in COMEX warehouses, leaving European and Asian physical markets critically short and prompting Codelco to offer a record $350/tonne premium for European 2027 deliveries.

headline: GOLDSTORM DRILLS 407m gold-silver at Crown Property on KSM-Treaty Creek trend — Golden Triangle BC junior hits continuous mineralisation
snippet: Goldstorm Metals (TSXV: GSTM) reported gold-silver mineralisation over a 407.55-metre interval in preliminary drilling at its 15,819-hectare Crown Property in British Columbia's Golden Triangle — on-trend with Seabridge Gold's KSM and Newmont's Treaty Creek deposits, two of the largest undeveloped gold systems in the world. Assays are pending; the 407-metre continuous mineralised length in early-stage drilling suggests a large coherent hydrothermal system rather than isolated veins, and the company has 15,819 hectares of prospective ground along the same structural corridor.

headline: CODELCO sets RECORD $350/tonne European copper premium for 2027 — tariff-driven COMEX hoarding strips global physical supply
snippet: Codelco, the world's largest copper miner, is offering European customers a record $350 per tonne premium over LME for 2027 copper deliveries — a direct consequence of US tariff-driven stockpiling that has concentrated over 70% of exchange-visible global copper inventory in COMEX warehouses, stripping physical supply from European and Asian markets. The record premium signals that real-world copper tightness is intensifying even as headline LME prices soften on inventory data that obscures a severe regional mismatch in physical availability.

headline: 17-YEAR MINE DROUGHT: Copper hits records but no major new supply can arrive before the 2040s
snippet: A Washington Times analysis finds that while copper prices have hit records, the mine development pipeline is so depleted that no significant new copper supply can reach market for roughly 17 years — far too late to bridge the gap as electrification drives demand. The piece contextualises the TC/RC collapse flagged by Friedland at LME Week: smelters are processing concentrate at negative charges because mine supply is structurally insufficient, a condition that sets the stage for prolonged elevated prices and a generational opportunity for junior explorers sitting on undeveloped copper deposits.

headline: OR ROYALTIES raises dividend 18% while producers fight AISC — royalty model captures gold upside without the cost bleed
snippet: Motley Fool Canada highlights OR Royalties (TSX: OR) as a standout beneficiary of gold's multi-year run: the company raised its quarterly dividend 18.2% to US$0.065 per share, delivering income growth that operating miners cannot match amid rising all-in sustaining costs, labour shortages, and energy cost inflation. The analysis positions royalty and streaming companies as the structurally superior gold equity when producers are consuming free cash flow to cover AISC inflation rather than returning it to shareholders.

headline: EARNINGS SURGE, STOCKS STALL: Gold producers post record margins but equities trade at historic discount to cash flow
snippet: Gold mining operating earnings have grown dramatically as spot prices surged through $4,000, yet producer equities trade at a historic discount to their own cash flows — a valuation gap that Sprott Asset Management says is now the widest on record. The analysis argues attention is shifting to margins and cash flow as Q3 2026 earnings season begins, with potential for sharp re-ratings in companies demonstrating cost control at current metal prices; Jefferies maintained its $5,000/oz 2027 gold target even as it trimmed near-term assumptions on rising real interest rates.

headline: VOLTA doubles Springer rare earth resource to 176Mt in Ontario — top-10 North American REE deposit eyes 2026 PEA
snippet: Volta Metals doubled the resource at its Springer rare earth and gallium deposit in Sturgeon Falls, Ontario — 56.6 Mt Indicated at 0.70% TREO plus 119.5 Mt Inferred at 0.58% TREO — placing Springer among the top-10 North American REE deposits by total contained metal per S&P Global data. Praseodymium and neodymium account for approximately 90% of net metal value; gallium (not yet captured in the resource estimate) adds critical-mineral optionality, and a Preliminary Economic Assessment is targeted for year-end 2026.

headline: AMERICAN URANIUM Lo Herma pump test hits 19.2 gpm — ISR scoping study assumption confirmed at Wyoming uranium play
snippet: American Uranium (ASX: AMU) confirmed that a 72-hour pump test at the Lo Herma in-situ recovery project in Wyoming's Powder River Basin sustained 19.2 gallons per minute — within range of the approximately 20 gpm assumption used in the company's scoping study. The result clears a key technical de-risking milestone before the next stage of economic study work on a project that sits in the world's most prolific ISR uranium production fairway, with spot uranium holding above $75/lb.

headline: ORPHEUS URANIUM maps 2.2km dual redox corridor at Frome — South Australia roll-front target footprint expands sharply
snippet: Orpheus Uranium (ASX: ORP) defined two parallel north-south redox corridors — Siccus East and Siccus West — each running at least 2.2 kilometres at its Frome project in South Australia's Curnamona Province, a classic roll-front uranium environment that hosted historic production. The definition of twin parallel corridors significantly expands the target footprint and supports a follow-up drill program designed to test uranium mineralisation within the sandstone host rocks traced between the two corridor margins.

headline: CERRO DE PASCO consolidates 100% of 75Mt Quiulacocha tailings — historic Peru copper-silver-zinc project fully secured
snippet: Cerro de Pasco Resources (CDPR) signed definitive agreements to acquire the remaining interest in the Quiulacocha tailings facility in Peru's Cerro de Pasco district, consolidating 100% ownership of a 75-million-tonne historic tailings deposit and securing all surface rights. The Quiulacocha tailings contain copper, silver, zinc, and lead accumulated over decades of processing at one of the world's historically richest polymetallic mining districts; consolidation positions CDPR to advance environmental remediation and metals recovery under Peru's updated tailings legislation.

headline: INDONESIA MORATORIUM LOOMS: NPI capacity freeze proposal adds structural supply floor under nickel market
snippet: Indonesia — the world's dominant nickel producer — is weighing a moratorium on new partly-processed nickel pig iron capacity alongside national ore quotas substantially below 2025 targets, a combination that sparked the week's 4.1% nickel price surge and raised structural questions about longer-term battery-metals supply. The proposed NPI cap matters beyond nickel: Indonesia produces critical inputs for EV battery supply chains, and any sustained output restriction would tighten the cost floor for the entire battery metals complex at a time when lithium prices are already depressed.
